kit.title: Your recovery kit
kit.intro: Your recovery kit is a list of 24 words. It is the only way back into your notes if this device is lost or you forget your passphrase: with the kit and a backup file, any computer can restore them.

security.scheduled.title: Scheduled backups
security.scheduled.intro: While atomik-kb is running and unlocked, it can write an encrypted backup into a folder you choose, every day or every week, and keep only the newest ones. Restoring one needs your recovery kit, as for any backup.
security.scheduled.needsFolder: Choose a folder first: scheduled backups are written there.
security.scheduled.keepHint: From 1 to 100. Older scheduled backups in the folder and in Google Drive are deleted; no other file is touched.
security.scheduled.keepError: Enter a whole number from 1 to 100.
security.scheduled.last.none: No scheduled backup has run yet.
security.scheduled.error: The backup could not be written: {message}
security.scheduled.saveError: The schedule could not be saved: {message}
security.scheduled.folderError: The folder could not be set: {message}
security.scheduled.drive.intro: While atomik-kb is running and unlocked, it can write an encrypted backup into a folder you choose, upload it to your Google Drive, or do both, every day or every week, and keep only the newest ones. Restoring one needs your recovery kit, as for any backup.
security.scheduled.drive.needsTarget: Choose a folder or connect Google Drive first: scheduled backups go there.
security.scheduled.drive.label: Google Drive
security.scheduled.drive.about: Upload each backup, still encrypted, to a folder named “atomik-kb backups” in your Google Drive. Google can see the file names, sizes and times and a small unencrypted header in each, but cannot read what you wrote.
security.scheduled.drive.connecting: Finish signing in in your browser…
security.scheduled.drive.disconnectBody: atomik-kb will stop uploading backups and forget this connection. The backups already in Google Drive stay there; you can delete them in Drive.
security.scheduled.drive.reconnectLabel: Google Drive needs you to sign in again
security.scheduled.drive.reconnectText: Google no longer accepts the saved sign-in, so backups are not reaching Google Drive.
security.scheduled.drive.noClient: This version of atomik-kb has no Google client built in. Open Advanced and enter your own Google client to connect.
security.scheduled.drive.ownHelp: atomik-kb signs in with the Google client built into this version. To use your own, create a “Desktop app” client in the Google Cloud console and enter its id and secret here. The guide “Setting up the Google client for Drive backups” lists the steps. Saving a client disconnects Google Drive.
security.scheduled.drive.doneBoth: Backup written to the folder and uploaded to Google Drive: {file}
security.scheduled.drive.error.consentDe: Google Drive was not connected: the notice was declined.
security.scheduled.drive.error.noClient: There is no Google client to sign in with. Open Advanced to enter your own.
security.scheduled.drive.error.browserTi: Signing in took too long. Try again.
security.scheduled.drive.error.denied: Google did not give access. Try again and allow atomik-kb to use its backup folder.
security.scheduled.drive.error.reconnect: Google no longer accepts this connection. Sign in again.
security.scheduled.drive.error.quota: Your Google Drive is full. Free some space, then try again.
security.scheduled.drive.error.notFound: The backup folder could not be found in Google Drive.
security.scheduled.drive.error.network: Google could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
security.scheduled.drive.error.server: Google had a problem. Try again in a little while.

sharing.share.title: Share “{name}”
sharing.share.intro: People you invite join this space through your sync server, each with a role. Everything stays encrypted: the server only learns who belongs to the space.
sharing.share.history: Everyone you invite receives this space’s whole history, including pages in the trash and everything ever deleted from them. Members keep copies; removing a member cannot take them back.
sharing.share.planError: Could not count what sharing would send: {message}
sharing.share.ai: Members may turn on local AI on their own devices; it then reads what they can read. AI stays off in a shared space until each member turns it on for themselves.
sharing.share.needSync: Turn on sync first (Settings, Sync): people join through your sync server.
sharing.share.needKit: Create your recovery kit first (Settings, Security): it gives you the identity other people see.
sharing.share.nameHint: Members see this name next to your changes. You choose it; they can check who you are with a safety number.
sharing.share.error.name: Type the name other members will see.
sharing.share.pending: Sending the space to your sync server...
sharing.share.done: “{name}” is shared. Invite people from Members and sharing.
sharing.share.error: The space could not be shared: {message}
sharing.members.title: Members and sharing
sharing.members.heading: Members
sharing.members.nameShared: Another member has the same name. Compare safety numbers to tell them apart.
sharing.members.viaKit: Added a device with its recovery kit on {date}
sharing.members.safetyHint: Compare these 30 digits with {name} in person or on a call you trust. If they match, you are talking to the right account.
sharing.members.removeBody: {name} loses access to this space and cannot read anything written from now on. They keep what they already received: past pages and edits stay on their devices. Everyone else gets a new key.
sharing.members.lastOwner: A space always keeps at least one Owner. Make someone else an Owner first.
sharing.members.pendingRekey: A member left: the key of this space is renewed with the next change.
sharing.invites.title: Invitations
sharing.inviteCode.title: Invite with a code
sharing.inviteCode.formIntro: You get a code and your server address to give to the person. They choose “Join a shared space” and type both, then you both compare six digits.
sharing.inviteCode.intro: Give the person this code and the server address. The code works for 10 minutes.
sharing.inviteCode.starting: Opening a session on the server...
sharing.inviteCode.waiting: Waiting for the person to type the code...
sharing.inviteCode.digitsIntro: The person typed the code. Check that they see these six digits, and ask them to confirm first.
sharing.inviteCode.check: They confirmed. Check once more that you both see these digits, then confirm.
sharing.inviteCode.done: {name} joined as {role}. You now see each other as verified.
sharing.pair.warning: Only confirm if the other person sees the same digits. Nobody from atomik-kb will ever ask you for them.
sharing.inviteLink.title: Invite with a link
sharing.inviteLink.intro: The first person who opens the link joins with the role you pick, once. They are not verified until you compare safety numbers. Send the link only to the person you mean.
sharing.inviteLink.once: This is the only time the link is shown. Copy it now; to share it again, create a new one.
sharing.inviteLink.webHint: Opens a page on your server that starts atomik-kb.
sharing.inviteLink.copyError: The link could not be copied. Select it and copy it by hand.
sharing.inviteLink.summary: The person joins as {role}. The link works until {date}.

sharing.join.error.code: This code is not right. It has 12 letters and digits.
sharing.join.error.account: Create your recovery kit first (Settings, Security): joining a space needs your account.
sharing.join.digitsIntro: Check that the person who invited you sees these six digits, then confirm.

viewLink.intro: A view link lets anyone read this page in a web browser, without an account.
viewLink.shows.title: What the link shows
viewLink.shows.page: This page only: not the rest of the space, and not its sub-pages.
viewLink.shows.text: The page as it reads now, with no history: text you deleted earlier is not in it.
viewLink.who.title: Who can open it
viewLink.who.anyone: Anyone who holds the link, with no account and no sign-in. Treat it like a password.
viewLink.who.server: The page is kept on your sync server, which also serves the viewer: its operator can read this one page.
viewLink.fresh: While a device of the space is online, the page follows your edits to within about a minute.
viewLink.once: This is the only time the link is shown, and it cannot be shown again. Copy it now; to share the page again, create a new link.
viewLink.publishing.note: The link starts to work once the page is uploaded, in a moment.

viewLink.error.noSync: Turn on sync first: a view link is served by your sync server.

sharing.close.body: Nobody can change the space after this. Every member keeps a read-only copy, and the server deletes its copy after 30 days. This cannot be undone.

formula.fn.if: Returns the second value if the condition is true, otherwise the third.
formula.fn.ifs: Tests conditions in turn and returns the value of the first true one; the last value is the default.
formula.fn.and: True when every condition is true.
formula.fn.or: True when at least one condition is true.
formula.fn.not: Reverses a true or false value.
formula.fn.empty: True when the value is empty, blank, 0, false or an empty list.
formula.fn.equal: True when two values are equal (like ==).
formula.fn.subtract: Subtracts the second number from the first.
formula.fn.divide: Divides the first number by the second.
formula.fn.pow: Raises a number to a power (like ^).
formula.fn.abs: The absolute value of a number.
formula.fn.ceil: Rounds up to a whole number.
formula.fn.floor: Rounds down to a whole number.
formula.fn.sign: -1, 0 or 1 for a negative, zero or positive number.
formula.fn.round: Rounds to the nearest whole number, or to a number of decimal places.
formula.fn.toNumber: Turns a text, a true or false value or a date into a number.
formula.fn.min: The smallest of the numbers or dates.
formula.fn.max: The largest of the numbers or dates.
formula.fn.median: The middle value of the numbers.
formula.fn.length: The number of characters of a text or of items of a list.
formula.fn.substring: Part of a text, from a start position to an end position.
formula.fn.contains: True when a text contains another text.
formula.fn.test: True when a text matches a regular expression.
formula.fn.match: Every part of a text that matches a regular expression.
formula.fn.replace: Replaces the first match of a regular expression.
formula.fn.replaceAll: Replaces every match of a regular expression.
formula.fn.split: Splits a text into a list at a separator.
formula.fn.join: Joins the items of a list into a text with a separator.
formula.fn.lower: Converts a text to lower case.
formula.fn.upper: Converts a text to upper case.
formula.fn.trim: Removes the spaces at both ends of a text.
formula.fn.repeat: Repeats a text a number of times.
formula.fn.padStart: Pads the start of a text up to a length.
formula.fn.padEnd: Pads the end of a text up to a length.
formula.fn.minute: The minute of a date, 0 to 59.
formula.fn.hour: The hour of a date, 0 to 23.
formula.fn.day: The day of the week, from 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday).
formula.fn.date: The day of the month, 1 to 31.
formula.fn.week: The week number of the year.
formula.fn.dateAdd: Adds an amount of time to a date.
formula.fn.dateSubtract: Subtracts an amount of time from a date.
formula.fn.dateBetween: The whole units of time between two dates.
formula.fn.formatDate: Writes a date as text with a pattern such as YYYY-MM-DD.
formula.fn.parseDate: Reads a date from a text such as 2026-10-18.
formula.fn.at: The item at a position, counting from 0 (negative counts from the end).
formula.fn.first: The first item of a list.
formula.fn.last: The last item of a list.
formula.fn.sort: Sorts a list in ascending order.
formula.fn.reverse: Reverses the order of a list.
formula.fn.unique: Removes the repeated items of a list.
formula.fn.includes: True when a list contains a value.
formula.fn.flat: Kept for Notion formulas; lists never nest here.
formula.fn.map: Computes a value for each item (current is the item, index its position).
formula.fn.filter: Keeps the items for which a condition is true.
formula.fn.find: The first item for which a condition is true.
formula.fn.findIndex: The position of the first item for which a condition is true, or -1.
formula.fn.some: True when a condition is true for at least one item.
formula.fn.every: True when a condition is true for every item.
formula.fn.count: The number of items, or of items for which a condition is true.
formula.fn.prop: The value of a property of this page (or of the page before the dot).
formula.fn.id: The id of this page or of another page.
formula.fn.name: The name of a person.
formula.fn.email: The email address of a person.
formula.fn.let: Gives a name to a value for use in an expression.
formula.fn.lets: Names several values, each seeing the ones before it.
